prioritized_defects.description: The diagram adds a 'create new space' and 'modify floor structure' flow directly under the missing asset type branch, but the requirement only authorizes these actions for IT group members after receiving an exception request from any administrative level.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R18 says IT group members can create a new space and modify floor structure when they receive an exception request from any administrative level. In the diagram, N25 is 'Send exception request' and then N26/N27 are performed by '[User]' rather than IT, with no explicit administrative-level trigger to IT.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Relabel and restructure this branch so IT group members perform the space/floor-structure changes only after an exception request from an administrative-level user.

prioritized_defects.description: The permission-change flow is incomplete: it only checks whether the new permissions exceed granted permissions, but it does not explicitly model delegation of another user or acquisition of the inventory administrator role.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R25 requires an administrative-level user to delegate another user to execute some or all authorized actions, and R26 says the delegated user acquires the role of inventory administrator. The diagram has 'Change permissions', 'Select user', 'Modify permissions', then 'Assign inventory administrator role' after a check, but no explicit delegation action or clear representation that the target user acquires the role as a result of delegation.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Model the delegation action explicitly and connect it to the delegated user's acquisition of the inventory administrator role.

prioritized_defects.description: The approval flow does not correctly model the required post-approval sequence: notification, waiting-for-execution list, and inventory update on receipt of the asset.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R20 requires email notification when the request is treated, R21 requires adding the request to the waiting-for-execution list, and R22 requires inventory update when the user receives the requested asset. The diagram shows display pending list -> approve request -> notify user by email, but there is no explicit step for adding the request to the waiting-for-execution list, and inventory update is only shown in a separate return-asset flow (N35-N38), not when the requested asset is received.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Insert a post-approval step to add the request to the waiting-for-execution list and show inventory update on asset receipt in the request workflow.

prioritized_defects.description: Authentication is not modeled with the required username-and-password input semantics for all users.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R23 states authentication is made by user name and password for all users. The diagram uses 'Enter credentials' and 'Login' without explicitly showing the username/password authentication step; this is a semantic loss because credentials are not clearly represented as username and password.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Replace or annotate the login input with explicit username and password entry.

prioritized_defects.description: The report flow does not distinguish the three required report types with explicit selection or production semantics.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R27-R29 require the system to produce an asset report by location, a request report, and a user permission report. The diagram shows generic 'Display report types' and 'Display report' with filter/sort, but it does not explicitly model the production of each of the three distinct report types.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Add distinct branches or labels for asset-by-location, request, and user-permission reports, and make the report generation step explicit for each.

final_recommendation: Fix the high-severity behavioral/semantic defects first, especially the hallucinated IT exception flow, delegation/role-transfer modeling, and missing approval post-processing, then address coverage gaps and duplicate-step granularity issues.
